title: Accounts Receivable Note — Invoicing, Due Dates, Late Fees and Payment Application on the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans
content:
Under the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans the premium is invoiced on the tier's billing frequency, and deductibles, surcharges, expedited shipping and transfer fees are invoiced as they arise. Each invoice falls due the tier's payment term after the invoice date, counted in calendar days with the invoice day excluded and the due day included, and an invoice unpaid past its due day carries the tier's late fee for each month or part month it stays unpaid. A deductible is billed with the claim it belongs to and is never netted against the claim payment, because the claim payment is made to whoever performed the work. Payments are applied to the oldest unpaid invoice unless the owner names one.

## What is invoiced, and when

| Charge | When it is invoiced |
|---|---|
| Premium | On the tier's billing frequency (annually, semiannually, quarterly or monthly, as the tier provides) |
| Deductible | With the claim it belongs to, as it arises |
| Extra claim surcharge | As it arises |
| Expedited shipping fee | As it arises |
| Transfer fee | As it arises |

## The due date as a quantity

The due date is the day reached by counting the tier's payment term in calendar days forward from the invoice date, the invoice day itself not counted and the final day counted; that final day is the due day, and payment on it is on time.

| Invoice date (hypothetical) | Tier | Payment term | Due date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | Parts & Labor Protection Plan | 30 calendar days | 31 March |
| 1 March | Total Equipment Protection Plan | 45 calendar days | 15 April |

## The late fee as a quantity

The late fee for one month is the invoice amount multiplied by the tier's late fee percent and divided by one hundred, stated to the cent; it is carried once for each month, or part of a month, the invoice stays unpaid past its due day. A part month counts as a whole month for this purpose.

- A 2400 USD premium invoice on the Major Component Protection Plan (1.25 percent per month) carries 30.00 USD for each month or part month it stays unpaid: unpaid for one month and ten days past its due day, it carries two months of late fee, 60.00 USD.
- The same 2400 USD invoice on the Parts Protection Plan (1.5 percent per month) carries 36.00 USD per month or part month.
- An invoice paid on its due day carries no late fee; an invoice paid the day after its due day has stayed unpaid past the due day for part of a month and carries one month of late fee.

## Deductible and claim payment kept apart

The deductible is invoiced to the owner together with the claim it belongs to. The claim payment goes to whoever performed the work, and the deductible is never set off against it: the owner is invoiced the full deductible and the payee receives the full claim payment.

## Payment application

A payment is applied to the oldest unpaid invoice on the plan. Where the owner names the invoice the payment is for, it is applied to that invoice instead.

## Figures this note reads

The billing frequency, the payment term in calendar days and the late fee percent per month are the tier's own figures under the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans.
